  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Writing behavioral reports}

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r setup}
library(quant2qual)
profile <- identify_archetype(mock_behavioral_data(200))
```

`write_behavioral_report()` assembles one document in a fixed, readable order:

1. **Key findings** -- dominant signature, friction-led share, classification
   confidence and outliers, in a highlighted box.
2. **Cohort synthesis** -- the cohort narrative, the archetype map, the
   signature chart, a summary table and a portrait of every archetype.
3. **Case studies** -- one narrative per selected case, each with its
   behavioral fingerprint chart.
4. **Methods** -- written from the classification settings: the scaling, the
   band edges in raw units, the archetype matrix and a reproducibility note.

## Formats

| `format` | Output | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `"markdown"` | pandoc Markdown (returned as text when `file = NULL`) | nothing |
| `"rmd"` | R Markdown source rendering with `quant2qual::neudata_pdf` | nothing to write |
| `"qmd"` | Quarto source declaring HTML and PDF formats | nothing to write |
| `"html"` | self-contained HTML in the Neudata palette | pandoc |
| `"pdf"` | PDF typeset with the Neudata LaTeX class | pandoc and LaTeX |

```{r markdown}
md <- write_behavioral_report(profile, ids = c(104, 105), style = "brief",
                              include_methods = FALSE)
cat(md)
```

Sources are written with their figures beside them, ready to edit:

```{r sources}
dir <- tempfile()
dir.create(dir)
write_behavioral_report(profile, file = file.path(dir, "study.Rmd"), format = "rmd")
list.files(dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

## The PDF house style

PDF output uses `neudata_pdf()`, an R Markdown format built on the Neudata LaTeX
class: a cover page with the client, reference and classification, branded
headers and footers, navy table headers, highlighted key-finding boxes and the
closing copyright page.

```{r pdf, eval = FALSE}
write_behavioral_report(
  profile,
  file = "onboarding-study.pdf",
  format = "pdf",
  title = "Onboarding friction study",
  subtitle = "Behavioral case studies from the March cohort",
  client = "Example Ltd",
  reference = "NDC-2026-014",
  confidentiality = "Confidential",
  pdf_style = "style1"
)
```

`neudata_pdf()` can be used by any R Markdown document:

```yaml
output:
  quant2qual::neudata_pdf:
    toc: true
    style: style2
client: "Example Ltd"
confidentiality: "Internal"
```

## LLM narratives

`narrator = "llm"` rewrites the case studies with `generate_llm_narrative()`
while keeping the cohort synthesis and methods rule-based. The fact sheet sent
for each case can be inspected first:

```{r facts}
narrative_facts(profile, 104)
```

```{r llm, eval = FALSE}
write_behavioral_report(profile, file = "study.pdf", format = "pdf",
                        narrator = "llm",
                        llm_args = list(reasoning_effort = "medium",
                                        instructions = "Write for a product manager."))
```

Numbers in the generated text that are not in the fact sheet are reported as a
warning and kept in `$ungrounded` on each narrative, and the rule-based draft
stays available in `$draft`.

## The R Markdown template

In RStudio, **File > New File > R Markdown > From Template > quant2qual
behavioral report** opens a parameterised report that reads a CSV, classifies
it and writes the narratives -- a starting point for studies that need more
than the automatic report. The same skeleton is available with:

```{r skeleton, eval = FALSE}
rmarkdown::draft("my-study.Rmd", template = "behavioral_report",
                 package = "quant2qual")
```
